join_table.text: Checker semantics: S6A owns the mathematical and code correctness of every checker function and reason code that S6B controls target. S6B judges each expectation against the byte-identical checker alias and the stated `why`; an expectation right for the code but wrong for the mathematics is reported in S6B as CONDITIONAL-J1.

Lifecycle limits: S6B owns RESOURCE-LIFECYCLE-PLAN and SCOPE-DESIGN limits and settlement; S6A owns the in-process enforcement code (Guard, deadline/cancel/signals, gate, publication, exit codes). Each slice flags a limit the other side's text claims but the code does not enforce.
Harness-checker interface: S6B owns every harness call into the checker (names, signatures, exception classes, report keys, guard modes) judged against the byte-identical checker alias.

Sun6 pinned inputs (run.json, orbits.jsonl.gz, rlp_duals.json, survivors.json) are not embedded; INPUT-PINS format survey, run.json claims and the real lines used by record_data/pipeline controls are author observations to be byte-checked by the parent before any run.

Sun5 pinned extract (635388 B) and the 37 fixture TSVs (each about 635 kB) are not embedded; each fixture must equal the pinned input with exactly the listed ops (fixtures-manifest sha256); the parent verifies by byte comparison before any control run.

Sun6 uses Sun(5) as an accepted import (verdict 2cf02436..., itself computer-assisted) in R1(6) and every hereditary test with |T| = 5; the Sun5 second-checker gate (slice S5FULL) is separate; a Sun6 PASS never discharges it and the full Sun7 gate needs both.

The written rules, lemmas, errata and format texts, R0/R1, minimality, Zhu Theorem 1.1, L0.6 and (Sun5) Lemma R and the S-D exclusion are not re-proved by any checker; the original and the second checkers share them, so errors in them are common-mode.

Launch, identity, signalling and settlement belong to the shared owned guard/supervisor, the parent five-part release, item GO and a fresh stability gate; none is reviewed here and no runtime authority follows from any verdict.
